propositions: Op-cert service performs per-job boto3/SSM/region lookup and patches process-global state, creating coupling and concurrency hazards that must be eliminated by moving key binding to startup.

Key material must be accepted at startup from exactly one of REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY, validated before queue/worker/network/workspace creation, copied to a 0700 directory with 0600 file permissions, and never reread except on restart.

Context-local signer, principal, and push-policy objects must be threaded through both job-producer signing chains (completion and plan-review) to replace global environment patching and ensure concurrent workers cannot observe or mutate each other's state.

The op-cert application runtime must have no SSM/boto3/region/key-parameter dependency; the deployment key must be materialized outside the app by fetch-secrets.sh and bind-mounted read-only with REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH.

Both out-of-opcert_service producer chains (completion via transition_close.sign_completion_verdict and plan-review via generation.sign_manifest) must accept and use an optional injected OpcertSigner binding when supplied by the service, while developer-local paths retain environment/genesis resolution as default fallback.

Process-owned key copy must remain stable for the process lifetime, be replaced only after restart, and cleanup must never alter the deployment source; Ed25519/DSSE algorithm, trust roots, producer, envelope persistence, and no-workspace-push invariants from ADR 0049 must be preserved.
